D BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www:dilg.gov.ph s. 204 OIL G OPINION Nn 08 RAMONCITO S. FERNANDEZ President and CEO Maynilad Water Services, Inc. MWSS Complex, Katipunan Ave. Balara, Quezon City Dear Mr. Fernandez: This has reference to your letter dated 12 February 2024 seeking the Department's assistance in causing the standardization of the fees that barangays charge prior to issuing clearances for projects or activities in their area. Per the representation, you are encountering varying requests relating to clearance applications for water pipelaying projects — from a fee of Php 500 per linear meter to a monthly fee of Php 25,000.00 until the pipelaying project is completed, and various requests for corporate social responsibility projects, e.g., donation of office tablets, chairs and printers, donations for the Barangay fiesta, to name a few. Thus, you are requesting for the Department's assistance in causing the cities/municipalities (especially those within the service area of Maynilad) to pass an ordinance that will prescribe standard fees for clearance applications with the barangays. At the onset, the grant of local autonomy is constitutionally mandated. Article X, Section 2 of the 1987 Philippine Constitution specifically provides for the grant of local autonomy to "territorial and political subdivision", viz: "SECTION 2. The territorial and political subdivisions shall enjoy local autonomy." However, the constitutional grant of local autonomy is not absolute. The Constitution likewise provides under Article X, Section 4 and Section 25 (a) of R.A. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 respectively provide: "SECTION 4. The President of the Philippines shall exercise general supervision over local governments. Provinces with respect to component cities and municipalities, and cities and municipalities with respect to component barangays shall ensure that the acts of their component units are within the scope of their prescribed powers and functions. Section 25. National Supervision over Local Government Units. - "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Trunkline: (02) 8876-3454

(a) Consistent with the basic policy on local autonomy, the President shall exercise general supervision over local government units to ensure that their acts are within the scope of their prescribed powers and functions. Xxxx" From the foregoing, this Department only exercises supervision over the local government units which is overseeing of the power or authority of an officer to see that subordinate officers perform their duties. If the latter fail or neglect to fulfill them, the former may take such action or step as prescribed by law to make them perform their duties. 1 In addition, the Chief Executive, through this Department, wielded no more authority than that of checking whether local governments or their officials were performing their duties as provided by the fundamental law and by statutes. He cannot interfere with local governments, so long as they act within the scope of their authority.2 As long as the LGUs are performing their functions within their scope of authority, this Department cannot interfere with the acts and duties of the LGUs. These LGUs determine what is best for their growth and development without undue interference or dictation from the central government.3 Thus, this Department cannot interfere or cause the cities/municipalities to pass an ordinance that will prescribe standard fees for clearance applications with the barangays as it will violate their local autonomy. This Department is precluded from interfering in local affairs so long as their acts are exercised within the sphere of their legitimate powers. However, you may consider writing to the Sanggunian Bayan concerned regarding the matter, since the said Sanggunian has the authority to pass an ordinance requiring the standardization of the fees that barangays charge prior to issuing clearances for projects or activities in their area. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same, and shall not be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY THORITY OF TH CRETARY: NV TOR R.
